title: Explain Client-Side Form Validation using JavaScript
summaryPoint: Validating user input within the client browser before submitting data across the network to the server.
keyPoints: Client-side validation verifies that required fields are filled, numbers fall within expected ranges, and email addresses or contact numbers match expected formatting.
It provides immediate user error feedback, prevents unnecessary HTTP requests, and significantly reduces server processing overhead.
Validation functions are commonly hooked using the form element's onsubmit event listener returning true or false.

title: Explain Event Handling and Common Event Types in JavaScript
summaryPoint: Events are browser or user interactions handled dynamically by invoking associated JavaScript functions.
keyPoints: onsubmit: Triggered when a user clicks the submit button to post form data.
onblur: Triggered when an input control or form element loses input focus.
onchange: Triggered when the value of a text box, select dropdown, or checkbox has been altered by the user.
onload: Triggered immediately when the browser finishes loading the full web page document.

title: Explain the Built-in String Object and Its Common Methods
summaryPoint: JavaScript built-in wrapper object providing methods for text manipulation and inspection.
keyPoints: length: Read-only property returning the total number of characters present in a string.
toUpperCase() & toLowerCase(): Converts all string characters into uppercase or lowercase letters.
charAt(index): Returns the single character positioned at the specified numerical index position.
substring(start, end): Extracts and returns characters between two specified index limits.

title: Explain the Built-in Math Object and Its Key Methods
summaryPoint: Static utility object containing mathematical constants and computational numerical functions.
keyPoints: The Math object is static; its methods are called directly without creating an object instance (e.g. Math.methodName()).
Math.sqrt(x): Computes and returns the square root of a specified positive number.
Math.floor(x): Rounds a floating-point number downward to its nearest integer.
Math.round(x): Rounds a numerical value to its closest integer based on standard rounding rules.
